newsitem.title: INDIA: India gold closes steady, silver up on thin supply.
newsitem.headline: India gold closes steady, silver up on thin supply.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed steady at 4,530 rupees per 10 gramme amid limited activity during the day.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) closed steady at 53,000 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees last week.
** Silver (.999) closed 30 rupees higher at 6,400 rupees per kg amid limited supplies and seasonal support.
Gold 24 carat closed steady at 4,530 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close amid limited supplies on Monday, dealers said.
Lower than expected seasonal buying coupled with narrow fluctuations in world prices kept local markets quiet during the day. Gold was down by 20 rupees per 10 gramme last week.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) closed steady at 53,000 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees last week.
"Sentiment was subdued at close despite approaching festivals on reports that Indian government is considering a proposal to liberalise import policy for gold," one broker said.

Silver (.999) closed 30 rupees higher at 6,400 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,370 rupees on the back of festival buying while limited supplies kept offerings at low ebb. Silver was down by 10 rupees on Saturday but was up by 75 rupees last week.
"Traders were expecting gold prices to remain quiet on Tuesday but silver may lose gained ground," a broker said.
